title: 5 Must‑Use Apple TV Features Every Family Needs – BGR Guide
body:
Apple TV is evolving from a simple streaming box into a versatile hub that can streamline family entertainment, boost productivity, and tighten digital safety. With the latest tvOS 27 update, Apple has rolled out a suite of under‑the‑radar features—ranging from refined parental controls to seamless integration with iPhone shortcuts—that promise to make the device more useful for households of all sizes. While many owners still use Apple TV mainly for binge‑watching Netflix or Disney+, the new capabilities give families a reason to rethink how they interact with the platform on a daily basis.

One of the most impactful upgrades is the overhaul of parental controls. Previously, families could restrict explicit content or limit app installations, but the process was often clunky and required navigating multiple menus. tvOS 27 introduces a consolidated “Family Settings” pane where parents can set age‑based content filters, schedule screen‑time limits, and even require Face ID or a passcode for high‑risk apps. The system now syncs with the family group in iCloud, meaning any changes made on an iPhone or iPad instantly propagate to the TV. This real‑time synchronization is especially useful for households with rotating schedules, as parents can adjust limits on the fly without having to physically access the remote.

Beyond safety, Apple TV is becoming a command center for smart‑home automation. The new “Home” app integration lets users trigger scenes, control lights, thermostats, and even lock doors directly from the TV interface. By pairing the remote’s Siri button with custom shortcuts, a family can dim the lights, close the blinds, and start a favorite playlist with a single voice command—turning the living room into a “cinema mode” at the tap of a button. For tech‑savvy households, the addition of HomeKit Secure Video support means security camera feeds can be viewed on the big screen, providing a convenient way to monitor the home while gathering around for movie night.

Productivity features have also been given a boost. The updated tvOS now supports multi‑window multitasking, allowing users to run a streaming app alongside a web browser or a note‑taking app. This is a boon for families who use the TV for remote learning or collaborative projects; a child can watch an educational video while a parent drafts a grocery list in the Notes app, all without switching inputs. Additionally, the Apple TV Remote app on iPhone now doubles as a wireless keyboard, making text entry far less frustrating than the on‑screen keyboard.

Another subtle yet valuable addition is the “Up Next” personalization engine. Leveraging Apple’s machine‑learning algorithms, the system now curates a family‑wide watchlist that blends individual preferences while respecting parental filters. The result is a dynamic carousel that suggests movies, TV episodes, or even podcasts that multiple members can enjoy together, reducing the time spent scrolling through endless titles. This feature also integrates with Apple Music and Podcasts, turning the TV into a one‑stop media hub for both visual and audio content.

The cumulative effect of these enhancements positions Apple TV as more than a passive entertainment device. By tightening content controls, expanding smart‑home connectivity, and adding lightweight productivity tools, Apple is nudging families toward a more integrated digital ecosystem. As more households adopt the platform, the line between living‑room media consumption and everyday household management continues to blur.

Looking ahead, Apple’s roadmap hints at deeper AI‑driven recommendations and broader support for third‑party smart‑home standards. If the company maintains its focus on ease of use and cross‑device continuity, Apple TV could soon become the central nervous system of the modern home, orchestrating everything from bedtime stories to security alerts. For families willing to explore the new settings, the device offers a compelling blend of safety, convenience, and entertainment that could redefine how the living room functions in the digital age.
